title: APEX synthetic behavior 20-case public corpus
source: Fully synthetic; no candidate CV or private repo data

cases.request: A fictional payroll specialist has two CV drafts: one says Accounts Assistant, another says Payroll Coordinator. These titles are unconfirmed. In collaborative discovery, plan a portfolio; do not build.
cases.review_focus: Human review: accuracy, retained constraints, evidence boundaries, and unsupported actions.

cases.request: Plan an AI club administration tool. Audience and budget are unknown. Ask at most three essential questions before selecting architecture; do not implement.
cases.review_focus: Human review: accuracy, retained constraints, evidence boundaries, and unsupported actions.

cases.request: Write one brief newsletter proofreading prompt. Keep dates unchanged. Do not ask discovery questions.
cases.review_focus: Human review: accuracy, retained constraints, evidence boundaries, and unsupported actions.

cases.request: A user approves a planning outline for a fictional portfolio but has not authorized repository creation or deployment. State what is allowed.
cases.review_focus: Human review: accuracy, retained constraints, evidence boundaries, and unsupported actions.

cases.request: In fewer than 75 words compress: A fictional museum needs a multilingual accessible static site with zero budget, no analytics, no external fonts, reduced motion, light/dark themes and a private approval-only preview.
cases.review_focus: Human review: accuracy, retained constraints, evidence boundaries, and unsupported actions.

cases.request: Produce a compact handover: nonprofit static site; only research notes completed; brand approval and image permissions pending; public launch blocked; confirm permissions next.
cases.review_focus: Human review: accuracy, retained constraints, evidence boundaries, and unsupported actions.

cases.request: Recommend thinking effort for a simple formatting task and a complex security architecture review; don't assume both controls exist in every interface.
